butter75g plain flour2 eggs75g gruyere, gratedTop the blinis with crème fraîche, smoked salmon and dill.Boil the water with the butter for the gougeres.Beat in the flour until the dough pulls away from the pan.Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the gruyere.Pipe small balls onto lined trays.Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.Arrange both on silver trays.Shell Cottage seaside crab toastsMayo and lemon crab on toasted sourdough fingersHow to make it250g crab meat3 tbsp mayonnaise1 lemon2 tbsp chives, snipped8 slices of sourdough bread1/2 tsp smoked paprikaFold the crab through the mayonnaise with lemon zest, a squeeze of juice and the chives.Toast the sourdough and cut into fingers.Pile the crab on top.Finish with smoked paprika.Tottenham Court Road café toastiesThe late-night café where the Death Eaters find themHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thick white bread toasted in butter around leg ham, melted vintage cheddar and a scrape of hot English mustard, cut into triangles.Butter the outsides of 8 slices thick white bread.Spread the insides of 4 slices with English mustard, then layer with 200g leg ham and 200g grated vintage cheddar and close with the other slices, butter side out.Cook in a frying pan over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes a side, pressing down with a spatula, until deep golden and the cheese runs.Cut into triangles and serve with a pickle on the side.Garlic butter field mushrooms on toastRon's Deluminator, clicking the lights out.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsFrozen pond foil baked trout with potatoesWhole trout stuffed with lemon, dill and butter, cooked in foilHow to make it4 whole trouts, cleaned2 lemons, sliced8 sprigs of dill60g butter, for the trout800g potatoes30g butter, for the potatoes1/4 cup parsley, choppedsalt and pepper, to tasteStuff the trout with lemon slices, dill and the butter for the trout, then season with salt and pepper.Wrap in oiled foil.Cook on a hot barbecue or at 200°C.Boil the potatoes until tender.Toss the potatoes in the butter for the potatoes and the parsley.Serve the trout in its foil.Godric's Hollow beef and grape juice pieChristmas Eve in snowy Godric's HollowHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beef chuck and onion simmered 3 hours in stock and grape juice, spooned into a dish under puff pastry and baked at 200°C for 25 minutes.Toss 1kg diced beef chuck in 2 tbsp seasoned plain flour and brown in batches.Soften 2 onions and 2 carrots in the pot, add 250ml grape juice and bubble 2 minutes.Add 500ml beef stock, 1 tbsp tomato paste and 2 bay leaves, cover and simmer 2.5 to 3 hours until tender.Cool a little, spoon into a pie dish and cover with 1 sheet puff pastry.Brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes.Serve with
